summary: Database joins leave `experimental`: `experimental: { joins: true }` is replaced by `advanced: { database: { joins: true } }` (default false)
The account table gains a required `issuer` column, and accounts are keyed on (issuer, accountId) instead of (providerId, accountId); 1.7.3 reverted this to (providerId, accountId) with no issuer

getAccessToken, refreshToken, accountInfo and unlinkAccount select an account by the local `account.id`, passed as `accountId`, or with `useAccountCookie: true`; `providerId` is removed from these selectors, and omitting both no longer falls back to the account cookie

The provider account id now comes from the raw verified profile (OIDC `sub`, plain OAuth `id`, or a new `accountSubject` option) with no runtime fallback; `mapProfileToUser` can no longer return `id`, `getUserInfo().user` no longer carries it, and `accountInfo` exposes it as `account.accountId` instead of `user.id`
The generic OAuth `microsoftEntraId` helper requires a concrete tenant GUID; `common`, `organizations` and `consumers` tenants are no longer accepted (use the built-in `microsoft` provider)
Microsoft accounts (built-in `microsoft` provider and the `microsoftEntraId` helper) are identified by the `oid` claim instead of `sub`, and tokens without a valid `oid` are rejected
The captcha plugin's `endpoints` entries must match full auth paths; partial prefixes such as `/sign-in` no longer cover `/sign-in/email` and need a wildcard (`/sign-in/*` or `/sign-in/**`)

The `mcp` plugin, `withMcpAuth`, `mcpHandler` and the in-core MCP client (`createMcpAuthClient`) are removed from `better-auth`; the plugin moves to `@better-auth/mcp` (`requireMcpAuth`, `createMcpProtectedRequestHandler`, flat options instead of `oidcConfig`, endpoints at /oauth2/* instead of /mcp/*)

OAuth provider access tokens bound to a session become inactive when the session ends: introspection returns `{ active: false }` and /oauth2/userinfo rejects them, where before they stayed valid until their TTL
The OAuth provider's `validAudiences` option is removed in favour of explicit `resources`; refresh tokens now use the shortest applicable TTL, and the `jwks` table gains `alg` and `crv` columns

SCIM provisioning no longer runs on the organization plugin: its configuration, client APIs, database schema and Group model are replaced, and existing state can't be migrated in place (full reprovision)
`enableTwoFactor` returns a discriminated response with a `method` field (`"totp"` with `totpURI` and `backupCodes`, or `"otp"`); callers must narrow on `method` before reading `totpURI`

With a dynamic `baseURL: { allowedHosts }`, the origin is resolved from `Host` and `x-forwarded-host`/`x-forwarded-proto` are ignored unless `advanced.trustedProxyHeaders: true`; requests with no usable or allowed host fail closed without `baseURL.fallback`
The device authorization plugin's `deviceCode` and `userCode` columns get unique indexes and a 191-character limit, so custom generators must return unique values of at most 191 characters
The device authorization `/device` endpoint gets a default rate limit of 5 requests per window equal to the code lifetime
Default-generated device user codes are now matched ignoring case and readability separators during verification, approval and denial (custom codes outside the default alphabet still match exactly)

The Electron sign-in flow requires S256 PKCE: the `code_challenge_method` parameter and the `disableOriginOverride` option are removed, plain PKCE is rejected, and the `electron-origin` header is no longer trusted

Custom-scheme `trustedOrigins` entries are matched by scheme and authority instead of string prefix, so a host-bearing entry like `myapp://callback` no longer matches `myapp://callback.attacker.tld` (host-less `myapp://` still matches any host)
The One Tap plugin refuses to verify ID tokens unless a Google client ID is configured via `oneTap({ clientId })` or `socialProviders.google.clientId`
Google One Tap binds accounts to the verified Google subject instead of matching existing users by email
The deprecated `oidcProvider` plugin is removed from `better-auth/plugins`; use `oauthProvider` from `@better-auth/oauth-provider`

Generic OAuth's dedicated client APIs are removed: `signIn.oauth2({ providerId })` becomes `signIn.social({ provider })`, `oauth2.link()` becomes `linkSocial()`, and the `genericOAuthClient()` client plugin is dropped
Generic OAuth providers use the shared callback route `/api/auth/callback/:id` instead of `/api/auth/oauth2/callback/:id`
Generic OAuth providers default `pkce` to true (was false); set `pkce: false` for providers that reject PKCE
Generic OAuth's `issuer` and `requireIssuerValidation` config options are removed; issuer validation comes from OIDC discovery
Generic OAuth's `authorizationUrlParams` and `tokenUrlParams` accept only `Record<string, string>`

Generic OAuth providers configured with `discoveryUrl` now verify the provider's id_token against its JWKS and bind it to a server-generated nonce, rejecting sign-ins that fail; set `disableIdTokenNonceBinding: true` for providers that don't echo the nonce

Custom `UpstreamProvider` implementations lose the `verifyIdToken` method; client-submitted id_tokens are checked by one shared verifier driven by an `idToken` config (JWKS, issuer, audience, or a `verify` function)
PayPal `signIn.social({ idToken })` now returns `ID_TOKEN_NOT_SUPPORTED` instead of accepting any decodable id_token; redirect sign-in is unchanged

`verifyAccessToken` from `better-auth/oauth2` (and the `oauthProviderResourceClient` action) is renamed `verifyBearerToken` and rejects DPoP-bound tokens; `AccessTokenRequestInput` is renamed `ResourceRequestInput`

The synchronous OAuth2 request builders `createAuthorizationCodeRequest`, `createRefreshAccessTokenRequest` and `createClientCredentialsTokenRequest` are removed; use the async `authorizationCodeRequest`, `refreshAccessTokenRequest` and `clientCredentialsTokenRequest`

SIWE nonces are issued before the wallet is known: `authClient.siwe.nonce()`/`getNonce()` no longer accept wallet address or chain ID, a server `getNonce` must return an ERC-4361 nonce (8–250 alphanumerics), and address and chain are read from the signed message
The public `generateState()` helper takes an options object, `generateState(c, options)`, instead of positional `(c, link, additionalData)` arguments
The OAuth callback redirect error code `email_doesn't_match` is renamed `email_does_not_match`
The public `getIp` helper export is renamed `getIP`
Custom `secondaryStorage` must implement `increment(key, ttl)` and `getAndDelete(key)`, which were optional before
Custom rate-limit storage must implement a single `consume(key, rule)` method; separate `get`/`set` storage is no longer accepted (in 1.6 `consume` was optional, with a fallback to get/set)
Magic-link and email-OTP sign-in to an account whose email was never verified now remove its unproven password and other linked accounts and revoke existing sessions before signing the user in

Signing out with `secondaryStorage` and `session.preserveSessionInDatabase` now runs `session.delete` hooks, marks the preserved session ended and revokes OAuth tokens bound to it; before, the hooks were skipped
The session cookie cache is tied to the `session_token` cookie, so cached session data is used only together with the matching session token
`organization.updateTeam` no longer accepts `id`, `createdAt` or `updatedAt` in the request body
`updateMemberRole` now validates that the role exists after the authorization checks rather than before, so an unauthorized caller gets the permission error first
A failed two-factor challenge cleanup returns the new error code `FAILED_TO_INVALIDATE_TWO_FACTOR_CHALLENGE`
Device authorization `/device/code` and `/device/token` responses (and OAuth credential responses) now send `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`

Built-in placeholder emails use `{identifier}@{namespace}.placeholder.invalid`, e.g. anonymous users get `{id}@anonymous.placeholder.invalid` and SIWE users `{wallet}@siwe.placeholder.invalid` (unless `emailDomainName` is set) instead of the old `temp@{id}.com`-, `.local`- or base-URL-domain formats
`getTestInstance` from `better-auth/test` uses a fast password hasher by default instead of the production hashing cost; a custom `emailAndPassword.password` still takes precedence

Better Auth validates the database schema at initialization by default, including in production, and rejects authentication requests while the schema doesn't match; opt out with `advanced.database.validateSchema: false`
The OAuth proxy plugin's legacy `/oauth-proxy-callback` endpoint is deprecated, to be removed in the next minor release

Passwords longer than `maxPasswordLength` are rejected with `PASSWORD_TOO_LONG` before hashing on sign-in (email, username, phone number), verify-password, change-password, delete-user, two-factor password endpoints and admin create-user, as sign-up and reset already did

Magic Link records and database-backed OAuth/SAML state are stored under separate verification identifier prefixes (`magic-link:`, `auth-state:`), and Magic Link verification accepts only Magic Link records; links issued before the upgrade stop working and `verification.storeIdentifier.overrides` rules must match the new prefixes

OAuth state cookies and OAuth Proxy payloads are encrypted with purpose-specific keys instead of the shared key, so sign-ins started before the upgrade and mixed old/new OAuth Proxy participants can't exchange state
